State of Play: Including Advanced Transmission Technologies in Power System Modeling Tools

Adria Brooks, PhD, Sophie Meyer, Julia Selker, Zachary Zimmerman

November 6, 2026

Technology

Advanced Transmission Technologies (ATTs) are tools that make the most of transmission corridors and infrastructure, allowing utilities to unlock additional capacity from the existing grid and enable grid flexibility, all at a lower cost than traditional grid upgrades. However, despite these technologies being commercially available, adoption has been slow.

FERC has previously required ATTs in grid planning through Order Nos. 1920 and 2023, but load growth is putting new pressure on these methods. In June, 
FERC orders to show cause
 asked regional transmission organizations whether they are using tools that can represent ATTs for load interconnection studies.

This new report from Grid Strategies attempts to help answer this question, reviewing the representation of Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs) and High Performance Conductors (HPCs)—collectively ATTs—in sixteen different commercial grid modeling software. As of fall 2026, most commercial grid modeling software can represent ATTs, but representation is uneven, and few software fully represent or optimize for the technologies by default. Ultimately, if the tools used to model and design the grid cannot test the applicability and cost-effectiveness of ATTs, engineers will not select them and potential benefits are undercounted or lost.
